correctness.rationale: The perimeter decomposition is exact whenever all edges are hit. Disjoint boundary endpoint intervals yield a jointly independent exponential limit; missing-edge events decay exponentially and endpoint order-statistic tails give uniform moments. The one-corner exact integral and near-origin expansion yield its linear coefficient; convolution yields the m-dimensional simplex coefficient. AM–GM with cyclic recurrence proves all equality cases. The verification script independently checks these formulas numerically, but analytic proofs carry infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Perimeter approximation of convex polygons is a natural intrinsic-volume error, and the small-error probability is a risk-sensitive accuracy criterion distinct from mean loss. The exact coefficient identifies all geometric and sampling parameters governing rare high-accuracy events; the sharp regular-polygon parity transition reveals a continuum of optimal designs for even order and unique uniform optimality for odd order. This is more than a routine numerical invariant and supplies a concrete design rule with explicit strict equality classification.
